text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a regression in prefix cache hit-rate after the recent kernel-selection tweak on rtx-pool. Short-sequence requests (<=64 tokens) p50 latency +8% and GPU mem foot-print uneven, seems correlated with fewer prefix hits.

aj: Oof. Any correlation to batching changes or the fallback path?

maria: I ran a small trace. Kernel selector now prefers fp16-fast path for model-v2 which changes kv key hashing early in pipeline. Suspect subtle key mangling during early tokenization -> different key prefixes.

cheng: Can you paste the trace snippet?

maria: Sure. Here's the sampling from a failing request (redacted):

```
REQUEST: id=abc123 seq=1 prompt="How do I..."
KVS: prefix_key=sha1:1a2b3c...
KERNEL PATH: fp16-fast -> kv_init -> kv_store.set(key=sha1:1a2b3c...)
NEXT REQ: prefix_key=sha1:1a2b3c... (but different salt) -> kv_get miss
```

samir: That different salt smells like tokenization normalization order changed. Maybe we moved whitespace trimming after kernel selection?

maria: Exactly. In the selector we call fast-normalize(token_buffer) which used to be post-kv-keying. Now it's pre-keying to choose kernels quicker. Saves ~0.6ms but breaks warmup.

aj: How big is the hit-rate delta?

maria: On 1h sample from rtx-pool: overall prefix hit-rate dropped 12 percentage points (76% -> 64%) for short seqs. For long seqs negligible. Cost delta ~ +9% GPU token compute due to regen.

cheng: Can we rollback the order in selector while we test a fix? Or detect stable-key vs unstable-key flows and route?

samir: Another angle: add a deterministic post-normalization canonicalization step before hashing, independent of kernel selection. Cheap and safe.

aj: I like canonicalization. Quick fix: insert `canonicalize_prefix(key_bytes)` before kv key derivation. Any perf penalty?

maria: Microbench: canonicalize ~0.05ms per request on CPU. With batching it's amortized. Worth it vs regen cost.

devops-bot: Deploy window available 01:00-03:00 UTC. Can run canary on 10% of rtx-pool.

cheng: Plan: 1) Add canonicalize step, 2) add unit tests for tokenization ordering, 3) canary deploy in dev and then prod 10%. If stable, keep selector change. If not, rollback order.

aj: Also add metric `kv_key_stability` that reports (% identical prefix_hash pre/post selector) — will help us detect regressions automatically.

samir: Also add eviction awareness: some of the misses are causing burst OOMs because we regen many prefixes and fill GPU cache. We should throttle regen into a soft-fallthrough queue when free_slots < 5%.

maria: Good call. I'll prototype canonicalize + stability metric today and a soft-regeneration throttle. Will post perf numbers after canary.

cheng: Small note for release: Include migration note in eng-runtime changelog and add a short blurb for support (they'll see increased misses during rollout if we don't canary carefully).

aj: Thanks. @maria if you need help writing the metric, ping me.

maria: Thanks — will @aj once I have the PR ready. :thumbsup:

samir: One more thought: for eviction/TTL tuning, let's add a short-lived "warmup bloom" — when we see a new prefix hit X times in 30s, promote it to protected TTL slot for 5m. Reduces fragmentation from transient prefixes.

maria: Noted. I'll include that as an experiment flag behind `exp/warmup-bloom`.

aj: Awesome. Keep this thread updated with PR and canary id.

maria: Will do. Last note: measured kernel-change perf win of 0.6ms is real, so goal is to preserve that by moving canonicalization to a zero-copy path where possible.

samir: Cool. Thanks team.
